papers_read.title_as_printed: Sequential patterning of dynamic brain states distinguish Parkinson's disease patients with mild cognitive impairments (Kemp et al., NeuroImage: Clinical 2025)
Identification of amnestic mild cognitive impairment by structural and functional MRI using a machine-learning approach (Hwang et al., Clinical Neurology and Neurosurgery 2024)

what_each_reports.P-145: Resting-state fMRI dFNC sequential-pattern classifiers (RF/LDA) in 22 HC, 18 PD-NC and 15 PD-MCI. The 0.80 is the upper end for HC vs PD (all Parkinson's patients regardless of cognition). PD-NC vs PD-MCI reaches 'up to 72%'. Moderate accuracies range from 0.53 to 0.80. Table 2 values are not recoverable from the extract (the table is rendered as an image).
what_each_reports.P-44: Amnestic MCI (n=50) vs cognitively unimpaired (n=26), single Korean hospital, linear SVM on FreeSurfer volumes (88.9%) and on volumes plus rs-fMRI graph metrics: accuracy 92.9%, AUC 0.929. 80/20 hold-out with 10-fold CV within training.

quantity_a: As cited: accuracy for healthy controls vs Parkinson's disease (any cognition) from rs-fMRI dFNC state sequences. Nearest MCI quantity: PD-MCI vs PD-NC within Parkinson's, up to 72%
quantity_b: Accuracy for amnestic MCI vs cognitively unimpaired memory-clinic patients from sMRI volumes + rs-fMRI graph metrics
incompatible_if_same: No. The cited 0.80 is a Parkinson's-vs-control accuracy, not MCI detection. P-145's MCI comparison (PD-MCI vs PD-NC, up to 72%) is within Parkinson's patients, whereas P-44 compares aMCI with cognitively unimpaired people. These are different comparisons in different populations, and neither study claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: the cited value is HC vs PD (disease detection, registry T4). PD-MCI vs PD-NC is a within-disease cognitive split, not the aMCI vs CU comparison of P-44.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: NYU Parkinson's cohort (OpenNeuro ds005892) vs Haeundae Paik Hospital, Busan
gates.modality_family: partial: P-145 rs-fMRI only; P-44's 92.9% combines structural volumes with rs-fMRI graph metrics (its sMRI-only result is 88.9%)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible endpoint (PD vs HC, or PD-MCI vs PD-NC, vs aMCI vs CU). Both report accuracy.
performance_validity: flag does not apply (no value at or above 0.97)
grounds: The record's claim_a misreads P-145: its 0.80 accuracy separates Parkinson's patients from healthy controls, not MCI from controls.

P-145's only MCI comparison is PD-MCI vs PD-NC within Parkinson's (up to 72%), a different population and comparison from P-44's aMCI vs cognitively unimpaired (92.9%), so there is no disagreement on a shared quantity.
The dataset gate fails and the modality gate is only partially met, with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: A machine-learning method using sequential pattern mining was also found to distinguish among the groups with moderate accuracies ranging from 0.53 to 0.80
distinguished people with PD from HC individuals with up to 80 %
as well as distinguishing PD-NC individuals from those with PD- MCI with up to 72 % accuracy
a total of 55 participants (all right- handed) were included in the current investigation: 22 in the HC group, 18 in the PD-NC group, and 15 in the PD-MCI group.
However, when the structural volumes and functional connectomic profiles were combined, the accuracy increased to 92.9%.
In addition, 26 CU patients were enrolled in the control group.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-145: Acc 0.80 on T1' is wrong: 0.80 is HC vs PD. P-145's registry row codes T4 with Best_Metric 'not reported'.
task_equal 'Yes' and dataset_equal 'Yes' are wrong: different comparisons and different cohorts.
resolution_note 'Same architecture family (A4_transformer)' is wrong: P-145 uses RF/LDA on sequential-pattern encodings and P-44 a linear SVM. Neither uses a transformer.
The bridging evidence (P-360, P-322) is generic.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these documents. A PD-MCI vs PD-NC result would still not be the aMCI vs CU quantity.
